hero.headline: AMC Relaunches Interview With the Vampire Series as The Vampire Lestat
hero.teaser: The network has rebranded its vampire series to focus on the title character, complete with original rock music and a premiere party concert performance.
hero.body:
AMC held a premiere party for The Vampire Lestat at New York's Beacon Theatre on June 2, where star Sam Reid performed six original songs from the series in character as vampire rocker Lestat de Lioncourt. The event featured Reid in full costume as the show's central character.

The relaunch transforms the series into a music-focused production featuring 20 original songs. The network has accompanied the rebrand with marketing tie-ins designed to promote the rock concert elements of the show. Reid, who does not perform professionally as a musician, trained for the role of the vampire turned rock star.

cards.headline: US Strikes Iranian Radar Sites After Intercepting Drones Fired at Bahrain and Kuwait
cards.body:
The United States military shot down four Iranian drones headed toward the Gulf and responded by striking Iranian coastal surveillance radar installations, prompting Iran to launch a fresh wave of attacks hours later. The exchange marks another serious test of the fragile ceasefire between the two countries.

On Saturday, air raid sirens sounded across Bahrain as residents were instructed to move to safe locations. Kuwait's military reported intercepting drones and missiles launched at the country. The Kuwaiti foreign ministry condemned the attacks as a "serious escalation" and "flagrant violation of its sovereignty," stating it reserved the right to defend itself.

US Central Command said the Iranian attack drones "posed an immediate threat to regional maritime traffic." The American strikes on radar installations at Sirik and Qeshm Island were intended to "defend against further attacks."

The Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed it had targeted American bases in the region, specifically stating it was aiming at the Ali al-Salem airbase in Bahrain, where the US Navy's 5th Fleet is based. Central Command reported that Iran fired seven ballistic missiles toward Kuwait and Bahrain, with six intercepted and one failing to reach its target. "There are currently no reports of harm to US personnel, and Iranian claims of damaging US 5th fleet headquarters in Bahrain are false," the command said.

This latest confrontation continues a pattern of back-and-forth military actions that have strained ceasefire negotiations. US and Iranian representatives have been working for weeks to extend the existing ceasefire by 60 days and begin new talks on Iran's nuclear program, but both sides have demanded changes to any deal.

President Trump said on Friday that "the situation with Iran seems to be going quite well" and predicted a quick resolution. "We're going to come out of Iran very quickly and it's going to be very strong one way or the other, whether it's a piece of paper or the very tough way," he said at an event in Wisconsin.

However, when asked why negotiations were taking time, Trump told NBC News it was "a very hard thing" for Iran. He also stated that Iran still possessed approximately 21 to 22 percent of its missile stockpile, slightly higher than the 18 percent figure he had cited the previous month.

The fighting threatens broader regional stability. Israel has also been striking targets in Lebanon despite a ceasefire deal brokered by the US this week. Lebanese President Joseph Aoun condemned an Israeli airstrike that killed nine people, including three army soldiers, calling it a "flagrant violation" of sovereignty. Israel said the vehicle was moving suspiciously toward its forces in an area where the Iranian-backed militant group Hezbollah operates.

Iran has demanded that any lasting truce extend to include Lebanon, complicating efforts to end the broader conflict and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial global shipping corridor.

cards.headline: Israeli Strike Kills Lebanese General and Two Soldiers Days After Ceasefire
cards.teaser: An Israeli attack on a vehicle in southern Lebanon killed a general and two other Lebanese soldiers, just days after a truce was signed.
cards.body:
An Israeli airstrike killed three Lebanese soldiers, including a general, when it hit a vehicle in southern Lebanon. The Israeli military confirmed the strike and said it is reviewing the incident.

The attack came days after Israel and Lebanon agreed to a ceasefire. Lebanese President Joseph Aoun condemned the strike as a violation of Lebanese sovereignty and international law. Israel has been conducting military operations in southern Lebanon against Hezbollah, but the operation has increasingly involved Lebanese security forces.

cards.headline: US Crude Oil Inventories Drop to Lowest Level Since 2004
cards.body:
American crude oil stockpiles have fallen to their lowest point in more than two decades, continuing a downward trend that reflects significant shifts in global energy markets. The decline underscores growing demand for US oil exports while domestic production remains constrained.

Commercial inventories have dropped as Gulf Coast export terminals ship record volumes of crude oil abroad. These facilities are moving oil at rates that exceed current domestic production and import levels combined. The drawdown marks the sixth consecutive weekly decline in stockpiles, signaling sustained pressure on reserves that have traditionally served as a cushion against market disruptions.

Energy analysts point to multiple factors driving the inventory reduction. Strong international demand for American crude, particularly as global markets navigate ongoing supply interruptions, has boosted export activity. At the same time, domestic production has not kept pace with outflows, creating a tightening situation in commercial storage facilities.

The Strategic Petroleum Reserve has also been reduced in recent years, adding to overall inventory pressures across the US energy sector. With less crude held in storage, the energy market has less flexibility to absorb unexpected supply shocks or seasonal demand fluctuations.

Despite historically low inventory levels, crude oil prices have not reached the elevated prices some analysts predicted. Several factors are moderating the price impact. Concerns about demand in major global economies are tempering expectations for sharp price increases. Additionally, crude production from non-traditional sources has helped prevent severe price spikes despite the tight inventory situation.

The gap between falling physical stock levels and relatively contained oil prices presents an unusual dynamic in current energy markets. Observers are noting this disconnect as a distinctive feature of how markets are functioning at present.

The depletion of commercial stockpiles carries real implications for energy security. With reduced inventory buffers available, markets face heightened sensitivity to disruptions. Supply interruptions or unexpected demand surges could trigger sharper price movements than would occur if reserves were more abundant. Commercial stockpiles typically provide crucial protection against short-term supply emergencies, and their decline reduces that protective capacity.

The trajectory of US oil inventories moving forward will depend on whether production increases or demand patterns shift substantially. Industry observers are closely monitoring market developments to determine whether the current tight inventory situation will persist or begin to ease.

The combination of strong export demand pulling crude out of the country and constrained domestic supplies suggests inventory pressures may continue unless significant market changes emerge. Energy analysts will be watching production trends, international demand patterns, and import volumes in coming months to assess whether commercial stockpiles begin to replenish.

cards.headline: Chip Sector Selloff Erases Over $1 Trillion in Market Value
cards.teaser: Major semiconductor stocks suffered their worst day in six years, with Micron shares dropping 13 percent.
cards.body:
The chip sector experienced a major selloff that wiped out more than $1 trillion in stock market value. Micron stock fell 13 percent, while Nvidia, Broadcom, and Marvell also posted significant declines in what analysts characterized as the sector's worst single-day performance since 2020.

The sharp drop affects some of the market's highest-performing stocks from recent years. Investors had poured money into semiconductor companies on expectations of strong demand from AI applications and data centers, making the sector one of Wall Street's most popular trades.

cards.headline: Trump Administration Discusses Government Stake in AI Companies
cards.teaser: The White House is exploring whether the federal government should take ownership positions in major artificial intelligence companies.
cards.body:
President Trump said his administration will explore the possibility of the U.S. government acquiring equity stakes in AI companies as a way for Americans to benefit from AI's success. The discussions involve OpenAI and other artificial intelligence firms, with meetings planned for the coming week.

The proposal has drawn interest from senators across the political spectrum, including Bernie Sanders, who have discussed public ownership models for AI development.

cards.headline: Trump administration discusses equity stake in OpenAI
cards.body:
President Donald Trump said his administration is in discussions about deals that would allow Americans to benefit from the success of artificial intelligence. The talks center on the government potentially taking an equity stake in OpenAI, the company behind ChatGPT and a leader in AI development.

The proposed arrangement would represent a significant shift in how the federal government engages with AI companies. Rather than simply regulating the industry, the administration is exploring ways to secure direct financial returns from AI advances. Trump framed the potential deals as a way to ensure American taxpayers share in the profits generated by AI technologies.

OpenAI has been valued at over 80 billion dollars in recent funding rounds and has attracted major investment from Microsoft and other tech companies. The company has been at the forefront of generative AI development, launching products that have transformed how businesses and consumers use technology. Any government equity stake would likely be structured through new agreements or investment vehicles.

The discussions come as the administration shapes its broader AI policy. Sriram Krishnan recently left his role as White House AI advisor, though he is reportedly starting a new institution to continue influencing the Trump administration's approach to artificial intelligence. The administration has signaled interest in both promoting AI innovation and ensuring American interests benefit from the technology's growth.

The potential for government ownership in a private AI company raises questions about oversight, conflicts of interest, and the relationship between Silicon Valley and Washington. How such an equity arrangement would be structured, what percentage stake the government might seek, and what governance rights would accompany any investment remain unclear.

The discussions represent an approach to technology policy that goes beyond traditional regulation or subsidy models. This marks a departure from conventional government involvement in the private sector, where policymakers typically choose between regulating industries or providing financial support rather than taking ownership positions.

The arrangement could have significant implications for how the government approaches technology policy moving forward. If pursued, it could establish a precedent for federal investment in other emerging technology sectors. The success or failure of any OpenAI deal could shape the administration's broader technology strategy and influence how future administrations view their role in the tech industry.

Questions remain about whether Congress would need to approve such a deal and what legal mechanisms would be used to structure government ownership. The proposal also raises broader questions about whether direct government ownership in a private company serves the public interest or creates potential conflicts that could undermine both government functions and commercial operations.

cards.headline: Israeli Soldier Kills Seven-Month-Old Baby in West Bank Shooting
cards.teaser: Israeli troops opened fire on a vehicle in the West Bank, killing an infant and wounding the child's parents.
cards.body:
A seven-month-old Palestinian baby was killed when an Israeli soldier opened fire on a vehicle in the West Bank city of Hebron on Friday. The infant's parents were also wounded in the shooting.

The Israeli military stated the soldier fired after troops perceived the vehicle accelerating toward them. However, the baby's grandmother, who was in the car, disputed this account. Israeli officials expressed "deep sorrow for any harm caused" and said the incident is under review. Palestinian officials condemned the shooting as Israeli forces continue operations in the occupied West Bank.

cards.headline: Israeli Strike Kills Lebanese General and Two Soldiers Days After Ceasefire
cards.teaser: An Israeli attack on a vehicle in southern Lebanon killed a general and two other Lebanese soldiers, just days after a truce was signed.
cards.body:
An Israeli airstrike killed three Lebanese soldiers, including a general, when it hit a vehicle in southern Lebanon. The Israeli military confirmed the strike and said it is reviewing the incident.

The attack came days after Israel and Lebanon agreed to a ceasefire. Lebanese President Joseph Aoun condemned the strike as a violation of Lebanese sovereignty and international law. Israel has been conducting military operations in southern Lebanon against Hezbollah, but the operation has increasingly involved Lebanese security forces.

cards.headline: Ukrainian Drones Strike St. Petersburg in Attack Russia Calls Unprecedented
cards.teaser: Russia described a Ukrainian drone attack on St. Petersburg as unprecedented, with the city's governor urging residents to stay indoors for the first time since the war began.
cards.body:
Ukrainian drones targeted St. Petersburg, prompting the city's governor to issue an unprecedented directive ordering residents to remain indoors—the first such warning since the war began. The strike on Russia's second-largest city represents a significant escalation in Ukraine's drone campaign, reaching deep into Russian territory.

In response to the attacks, President Vladimir Putin announced Russia would strengthen its air defenses. The drone strikes cast a shadow over Putin's economic forum being held in his hometown of St. Petersburg.

cards.headline: CIA Officer Accused of Fake Spy Program and Embezzlement Ordered Held in Detention
cards.teaser: A federal judge ruled that CIA employee David Rush must remain in custody over allegations he created a fraudulent intelligence program and funneled millions in federal funds to himself.
cards.body:
David Rush, a CIA officer found in possession of gold bars, must remain in detention while facing federal charges, a judge ruled. US officials allege Rush created a fake spy program and embezzled millions of dollars in government funds for personal gain.

The case involves allegations that Rush used his position within the intelligence agency to establish a fraudulent operation that allowed him to divert federal money. Authorities discovered gold bars during their investigation into Rush's activities. The judge's decision to keep Rush in custody suggests prosecutors presented evidence he poses a flight risk or danger to the community.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary Hegseth Invokes Immigration as Invasion in D-Day Speech in France
cards.teaser: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth used a D-Day anniversary ceremony in France to urge Europe to counter what he called a present-day invasion through immigration.
cards.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth delivered remarks at a D-Day commemoration in France that linked current immigration patterns to invasion. He urged European nations to address what he described as dangerous ideologies entering through migration, while calling on allies to increase defense spending.

The speech departed from typical D-Day anniversary addresses, which traditionally focus on the World War II battle and the U.S.-Europe alliance. Hegseth's characterization of migration as an invasion of European beaches generated criticism from observers who felt the remarks were inappropriate for the solemn occasion.

cards.headline: Pope Leo Begins Spain Visit With Praise for Government Amid Conservative Opposition
cards.teaser: Pope Leo arrived in Spain for a weeklong visit where he praised the government and is expected to meet with migrants, potentially drawing criticism from the far-right Vox party.
cards.body:
Pope Leo began his weeklong visit to Spain on Saturday with calls for political unity and rejection of polarization. In his opening speech, he urged leaders to seek consensus rather than divide populations for political gain, and emphasized the need to fight for peace.

The pontiff has prioritized meetings with marginalized communities during this first EU tour since 2012, including visits with homeless people in Madrid and migrants in the Canary Islands. He has also stated that the war in Iran does not qualify as a "just war" under Catholic teaching. His visit comes amid tensions with Spain's conservative factions, particularly the far-right Vox party.

hero.headline: Auburn University student found dead in Japan after days-long search
hero.body:
An Auburn University student who went missing in Japan has been found dead, according to his mother. The discovery came after several days of intensive searching by Japanese authorities.

The student's mother confirmed the death and described it as an "unimaginable loss." She revealed to reporters that she and her son had argued over ChatGPT before he disappeared. Investigators are still working to determine what role, if any, this disagreement played in the circumstances surrounding his death.

The student had been hiking in Japan when he went missing. Japanese authorities launched a search operation in the area where he was last seen, with the effort involving coordination between American and Japanese officials. The international cooperation reflected the complexity of handling a missing persons case involving a foreign national.

The exact circumstances of the death have not been fully disclosed by Japanese authorities. While the student's identity has been confirmed through multiple news reports, details about how and where he died remain under investigation. Japanese officials are continuing their work to piece together what happened during the period when the student was missing.

Auburn University has not yet released an official statement about the death. The university community is likely to be significantly affected by the loss of one of its students while studying or traveling abroad.

The case has drawn considerable attention in both the United States and Japan due to its international nature and the circumstances involved. The tragedy highlights the risks that can accompany international travel and the challenges families face when loved ones go missing abroad.

Family members were actively awaiting updates throughout the search period before receiving the confirmation they had been dreading. The death marks a tragic conclusion to what had been an active search effort involving local Japanese authorities and coordination with American officials. During the days when the student was missing, emergency responders and search teams worked to locate him in the hiking area where he was last known to be.

The case has raised questions about what led to the argument between mother and son over ChatGPT and whether there were other factors contributing to his disappearance. These details may become clearer as the investigation progresses and Japanese authorities release more information about their findings.

The death serves as a sobering reminder of how quickly circumstances can change for travelers abroad and the importance of safety precautions when engaging in outdoor activities in unfamiliar locations. As the investigation continues, both American and Japanese officials are likely to examine all available evidence to determine the full circumstances of what happened to the Auburn student.

cards.headline: Trump pardons former Republican congressman convicted of insider trading
cards.teaser: President Trump issued a pardon to Stephen Buyer, a former Republican congressman who had been convicted of insider trading.
cards.body:
President Trump granted a pardon to Stephen Buyer, a former Republican congressman who was convicted of insider trading. The pardon was issued quietly following a Supreme Court decision that did not favor the former lawmaker.

Buyer had been found guilty of using insider information for stock trading during his time in Congress. Multiple news outlets reported the pardon, which came without significant advance notice or public ceremony from the White House.

cards.headline: Witness testifies in Karmelo Anthony murder trial about seeing victim's injury
cards.teaser: A witness in the Karmelo Anthony murder trial testified that he saw the victim lift his shirt to reveal a large wound.
cards.body:
Testimony continued in the murder trial of Karmelo Anthony, with a witness describing the immediate aftermath of a fatal stabbing. The witness told the court he saw victim Austin Metcalf lift his shirt to reveal a big hole from the wound.

The jury also viewed video footage showing the chaotic scene following the stabbing, which occurred at a track meet. Witnesses testified about the confrontation that led to Metcalf's death. The trial has featured testimony from teenage witnesses who were present during the incident.

cards.headline: Pope Leo says Iran conflict does not meet criteria for just war
cards.teaser: Pope Leo XIV stated that the war in Iran does not qualify as a just war under Catholic teaching.
cards.body:
Pope Leo XIV said the war in Iran does not qualify as a "just war" according to Catholic teaching. He made the comments while responding to journalists aboard the papal plane during his six-day visit to Spain.

The pope has emphasized unity and peace throughout his tour, urging political leaders to reject polarization and division. He has made the marginalized a focus of his visit, meeting with homeless people in Madrid and migrants in the Canary Islands. The pope has previously clashed with U.S. President Donald Trump over immigration policies and the conflict with Iran.

cards.headline: Some Republicans defying Trump agenda as midterm elections approach
cards.teaser: A growing number of Republican lawmakers are breaking with President Trump on key issues as midterm elections draw closer.
cards.body:
Vulnerable Republican members of Congress have increasingly opposed President Trump's agenda in recent weeks as they prepare for midterm elections. Facing pressure from their home districts, some lawmakers have chosen to distance themselves from the president.

Political analysts have debated the motivations behind these breaks, questioning whether Republicans are acting on principle or making strategic calculations for competitive races ahead.

cards.headline: Teenager Mirra Andreeva wins first Grand Slam title at French Open
cards.teaser: Teenage tennis player Mirra Andreeva captured her first Grand Slam championship by defeating qualifier Maja Chwalinska at the French Open.
cards.body:
Mirra Andreeva has won her first Grand Slam title at the French Open, defeating Polish qualifier Maja Chwalinska in the final. The teenage player's victory represents the realization of the considerable potential that had long been recognized by tennis observers.

The triumph came at the expense of Chwalinska's fairytale run through the tournament. The qualifier's path to the French Open final came to an end with the loss to Andreeva at Roland Garros in Paris.

cards.headline: Ukrainian drones strike St Petersburg in attack Russia calls unprecedented
cards.teaser: Ukrainian drones targeted St Petersburg in what Russian officials described as an unprecedented attack on the city.
cards.body:
Ukrainian drones struck St Petersburg in an attack that Russian officials described as unprecedented in scale. The strike prompted the city's governor to issue an unprecedented directive for residents to remain indoors—the first such instruction since the war began.

The attack underscores the expanding reach of Ukrainian drone operations into Russia's heartland. President Vladimir Putin responded by pledging to strengthen Russia's air defenses against the drone attacks, which have penetrated deep into Russian territory and disrupted his economic forum in St Petersburg.

cards.teaser: Major semiconductor stocks suffered their worst day in six years, with Micron shares dropping 13 percent.
cards.body:

The sharp drop affects some of the market's highest-performing stocks from recent years. Investors had poured money into semiconductor companies on expectations of strong demand from AI applications and data centers, making the sector one of Wall Street's most popular trades.

cards.headline: States Prepare Lawsuit to Block Paramount-Warner Bros Merger
cards.teaser: Multiple US states plan legal action to prevent the $110 billion merger of Paramount and Warner Bros Discovery.
cards.body:
State attorneys general are preparing to sue to block the merger between Paramount and Warner Bros Discovery, adding to regulatory challenges facing the $110 billion deal. Paramount has asked a judge to dismiss a separate antitrust lawsuit filed by consumers seeking to stop the combination.

In Europe, Paramount has indicated willingness to sell some children's channels to address European Union competition concerns. The company is navigating regulatory reviews on multiple continents as it seeks approval for what would be one of the largest media mergers in recent years.

cards.headline: SpaceX Sets IPO Price at $135 Per Share
cards.teaser: SpaceX told underwriting banks it will not move from its planned initial public offering price of $135 per share.
cards.body:
SpaceX is proceeding with its IPO at $135 per share on June 12, planning to sell 555.6 million shares and raise $75 billion—positioning it as the largest stock market launch in history.

Up to a quarter of the shares will be reserved for individual retail investors, a significantly larger allocation than typical for major IPOs. Meanwhile, the company has secured a $920 million monthly deal with Google for compute services, driven by demand for Google's recently launched AI products.

cards.headline: Target Recalls Baby Wipes Over Bacterial Contamination
cards.teaser: Target is voluntarily recalling two types of baby wipes after finding bacteria that could cause serious infections.
cards.body:
Target issued a voluntary recall of two baby wipe products after testing revealed contamination with bacteria that can cause life-threatening infections including sepsis. The recall affects specific lots of Target-branded wipes sold at the retailer's stores.

The bacteria detected in the products poses particular risk to infants and individuals with compromised immune systems. Target has not disclosed how many units are affected by the recall or when the contamination was discovered.

cards.headline: Cattle Ranchers Face Screwworm Outbreak and Drought
cards.teaser: Texas ranchers are confronting the possibility of a screwworm outbreak while drought conditions force early cattle sales.
cards.body:
Texas cattle ranchers are confronting a serious screwworm outbreak alongside persistent drought conditions. A second infected calf was confirmed by the US Department of Agriculture, prompting Governor Greg Abbott to declare a state of disaster. The parasitic flies lay eggs that develop into larvae feeding on living flesh, posing a severe threat to livestock.

State and federal officials are working to contain the outbreak, including releasing sterile flies to slow reproduction. The crisis has prompted Canada to ban cattle imports from Texas. Combined with insufficient grazing grass from drought, ranchers face mounting financial pressure as they manage disease prevention while struggling to feed their herds.

cards.headline: Sriram Krishnan leaves White House AI advisor role
cards.teaser: The advisor is departing to start a new institution focused on shaping AI policy.
cards.body:
Sriram Krishnan has left his position as White House AI advisor under the Trump administration. The departure marks a shift in the administration's AI policy team as it continues to develop its approach to artificial intelligence regulation and promotion.

Krishnan is reportedly starting a new institution that will continue to influence the Trump administration's AI policy from outside government. The move suggests he will maintain involvement in shaping federal AI strategy through a different organizational structure.

cards.headline: Apple prepares to unveil Siri revamp at WWDC
cards.teaser: The company's developer conference approaches with AI features expected.
cards.body:
Apple is preparing for its Worldwide Developers Conference, where the company is expected to announce significant updates to Siri and Apple Intelligence. The conference represents a key moment for the company's AI strategy as it seeks to compete with other tech companies in artificial intelligence.

The event will showcase iOS 27 and other software updates. Observers are watching to see how Apple integrates AI capabilities into its ecosystem and whether the updates will address criticisms that the company has lagged behind competitors in AI development.

cards.headline: AI finds over 800 undocumented objects in Hubble archive
cards.teaser: Artificial intelligence discovered previously unnoticed astronomical objects in 35 years of telescope images.
cards.body:
An AI system analyzed 35 years of Hubble Space Telescope images and discovered over 800 previously undocumented objects. The finding reveals that despite decades of human examination, significant discoveries remained unnoticed in one of astronomy's most extensively studied archives.

The AI's success at identifying patterns and anomalies in large image datasets demonstrates the potential for machine learning tools to extract additional scientific value from existing astronomical data. This approach could help accelerate discoveries across other scientific archives as well.

cards.headline: Air filters capture DNA that identifies nearby wildlife and viruses
cards.teaser: Scientists found that atmospheric DNA collection can detect organisms in the surrounding area.
cards.body:
Scientists have discovered that air filters can capture DNA floating in the atmosphere, enabling them to identify wildlife, viruses, and plants linked to drugs in nearby areas. This breakthrough demonstrates that airborne genetic material becomes trapped in filtration systems, providing researchers with a practical tool for environmental monitoring.

The technique offers a passive surveillance method for tracking species and pathogens in specific locations. By analyzing the DNA collected through standard air filters, scientists can create a snapshot of the biological activity present in an area, opening new applications for biosecurity and environmental assessment.

cards.headline: Sea star populations rebound after massive die-off
cards.teaser: A biologist has observed a surprising baby boom following the species decline.
cards.body:
After a massive die-off of sea stars, a biologist has documented a surprising baby boom in the species population. The observation suggests the marine animals may be recovering from the catastrophic decline that devastated their numbers.

The die-off had raised concerns about the long-term survival of sea star populations in affected regions. The unexpected surge in juvenile sea stars offers hope that the species can rebuild, though scientists continue to monitor whether the recovery will be sustained.

cards.headline: Ancient microbes frozen with Ötzi the Iceman still viable
cards.teaser: Some microorganisms preserved with the 5,300-year-old mummy remain capable of growth.
cards.body:
Some ancient microbes that were frozen alongside Ötzi the Iceman are still growing, scientists have found. The discovery raises questions about the boundary between a person, an artifact, and an ecosystem, as the preserved biological material continues to exhibit life processes.

Ötzi, discovered in the Alps in 1991, has been preserved in ice for approximately 5,300 years. The finding that microorganisms associated with the mummy remain viable after millennia of freezing has implications for understanding microbial resilience and the nature of long-term biological preservation.

hero.headline: Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva wins French Open for first Grand Slam title
hero.body:
Mirra Andreeva claimed her first Grand Slam title at the French Open, defeating Polish qualifier Maja Chwalinska in the final. The Russian teenager fulfilled her considerable potential with the victory at Roland-Garros, ending Chwalinska's run through the tournament.

Chwalinska entered the final as a qualifier seeking a fairytale ending to her improbable run through the draw. The Polish player fell short against Andreeva, who proved the stronger competitor in the championship match.

The victory marks a breakthrough moment for Andreeva, who has been regarded as one of tennis's most promising young players. Her win adds her name to the list of Grand Slam champions and represents the culmination of her rapid rise through professional tennis.

The French Open title is Andreeva's first major championship at the highest level of tennis. The teenager's performance throughout the tournament demonstrated the talent that has made her one of the sport's most watched emerging stars. Her win at Roland-Garros puts her among the youngest Grand Slam champions in recent tennis history.

The final brought an end to Chwalinska's remarkable tournament run as a qualifier. The Polish player had navigated through the qualifying rounds and main draw to reach her first Grand Slam final, but could not overcome Andreeva in the championship match. Andreeva's victory caps a tournament that showcased both players' abilities on clay at one of tennis's most prestigious venues.

cards.headline: Kimi Antonelli takes pole position at Monaco Grand Prix
cards.teaser: Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli secured pole position for the Monaco Grand Prix, edging out Max Verstappen with Lewis Hamilton qualifying third.
cards.body:
The 19-year-old Mercedes driver claimed pole position at Monaco, edging out Red Bull's Max Verstappen by just 0.043 seconds in a thrilling qualifying session. Lewis Hamilton secured third place for Ferrari, while George Russell finished sixth.

Antonelli's performance was particularly impressive given he defeated two highly experienced rivals with 11 world titles between them on Monaco's challenging single-lap format. With overtaking nearly impossible on the principality's tight streets, qualifying proved decisive and dramatic, with the Mercedes driver delivering a flawless lap to take the advantage into Saturday's race.

cards.headline: England five wickets from Test win over New Zealand after rain-affected day
cards.teaser: England moved closer to victory over New Zealand in the first Test at Lord's despite rain limiting play on the third day.
cards.body:
England moved closer to victory over New Zealand on a rain-disrupted third day at Lord's. With just 58 legal deliveries possible, the hosts made the most of limited playing time to strengthen their position. Ollie Robinson played a key role in the bowling effort as England advanced toward the win they need in this first Test.

Rain repeatedly interrupted play throughout the day, eventually forcing an early end to proceedings. England require five more wickets to secure victory, with the match set to continue into day four.

cards.headline: USMNT faces Germany in final World Cup send-off match
cards.teaser: The United States men's national team played Germany in their final friendly before the World Cup.
cards.body:
The United States men's national team played Germany in the Coca-Cola Send-Off Match, their final preparation game before the World Cup. Head coach Mauricio Pochettino used the friendly to assess tactics and personnel ahead of the tournament.

Defender Chris Richards missed the match due to an ankle injury, with his World Cup status now in doubt. Pochettino indicated further assessments would be needed to determine whether Richards could participate in the World Cup.

cards.headline: Exeter reaches Premiership playoffs with win over Saracens
cards.teaser: Exeter defeated Saracens 32-12 to secure a Premiership playoff semi-final spot and bring an end to Mark McCall's tenure as Saracens head coach.
cards.body:
Exeter secured their place in the Premiership playoff semi-finals with a 32-12 victory over rivals Saracens. The win marks Exeter's return to the top four for the first time since 2021, ending a five-year absence from the playoffs. The Chiefs will face Bath at the Rec in next Saturday's semi-final.

The defeat concluded Mark McCall's 15-year tenure as Saracens head coach. McCall's long reign came to an end as his side fell short in the race for a playoff spot, with Exeter's superior physicality and endurance proving decisive in the intense encounter between the two bitter rivals.

cards.headline: Arsenal approach PSG for teenage defender Emmanuel Mbemba
cards.teaser: Arsenal made an approach to sign Paris St-Germain teenage defender Emmanuel Mbemba on a free transfer this summer.
cards.body:
Arsenal have made an approach to Paris St-Germain regarding teenage defender Emmanuel Mbemba, with the move potentially happening on a free transfer this summer.

The move would allow Arsenal to add defensive depth to their squad by acquiring a young prospect from the French club.

cards.headline: NASCAR Cup and Truck Series return to Michigan International Speedway
cards.teaser: NASCAR's Cup and Truck Series returned to Michigan International Speedway for race weekend.
cards.body:
The NASCAR Cup Series and Truck Series returned to Michigan International Speedway for race weekend. Denny Hamlin and Tyler Reddick continued their championship battle at the two-mile oval track.

Hamlin was favored by oddsmakers heading into the Michigan race, with Christopher Bell also garnering attention from betting markets. Pit stall assignments were announced in advance of the weekend's competition.

hero.headline: AMC Relaunches Interview With the Vampire Series as The Vampire Lestat
hero.teaser: The network has rebranded its vampire series to focus on the title character, complete with original rock music and a premiere party concert performance.
hero.body:
AMC held a premiere party for The Vampire Lestat at New York's Beacon Theatre on June 2, where star Sam Reid performed six original songs from the series in character as vampire rocker Lestat de Lioncourt. The event featured Reid in full costume as the show's central character.

The relaunch transforms the series into a music-focused production featuring 20 original songs. The network has accompanied the rebrand with marketing tie-ins designed to promote the rock concert elements of the show. Reid, who does not perform professionally as a musician, trained for the role of the vampire turned rock star.

cards.headline: Scary Movie 6 Opens With $24.7 Million on First Day
cards.teaser: The first Scary Movie installment directed by the Wayans brothers since 2001 is on pace to set a franchise record after a strong opening day.
cards.body:
"Scary Movie 6" earned $24.7 million domestically on its opening Friday across 3,490 theaters. The horror comedy marks the first installment in the Wayans brothers' parody franchise since 2001's "Scary Movie 2," released jointly by Paramount and Miramax.

The strong opening day performance positions the film to potentially set a franchise record by the end of the weekend. "Masters of the Universe" claimed second place with $11.7 million in Friday ticket sales.

cards.headline: Patrick Godfrey, English Actor Known for Ever After, Dies at 93
cards.teaser: Patrick Godfrey, the English actor who portrayed Leonardo da Vinci in the 1998 fantasy film Ever After: A Cinderella Story, died Thursday at age 93.
cards.body:
Patrick Godfrey, the English actor best remembered for playing Leonardo da Vinci in the 1998 film Ever After: A Cinderella Story, has died at age 93. His talent agency, Markham Froggatt Irwin, announced his death on June 5.

Godfrey had a long career in British television and film, with notable roles in Doctor Who, The Bill, and adaptations of Les Misérables and The Count of Monte Cristo. In Ever After, he portrayed the Renaissance artist as both narrator and mentor to Drew Barrymore's Cinderella. He died surrounded by family.

cards.headline: Scorsese, De Niro, Foster Reunite to Mark 50 Years of Taxi Driver
cards.teaser: The director, star, and supporting actress gathered to commemorate the half-century anniversary of the 1976 film.
cards.body:
Martin Scorsese, Robert De Niro, and Jodie Foster reunited to celebrate the 50th anniversary of Taxi Driver, the 1976 film written by Paul Schrader. Foster recalled that Scorsese and De Niro struggled to maintain composure while teaching her how to unzip a fly during filming, saying they were nervous during the scene.

The reunion brought together key figures from the production to reflect on the film's creation and legacy. Schrader, who wrote the screenplay, also participated in the anniversary events. The discussions touched on the film's themes of isolation and obsession, which the participants noted remain present in contemporary society.

cards.headline: The Cure Plays Rare Songs at First Concert Since November 2024
cards.teaser: Robert Smith and the band performed deep cuts including 2 Late, Wrong Number, and Mint Car during their Primavera Sound headlining set.
cards.body:
The Cure performed at Primavera Sound in their first concert appearance since November 2024. The band, led by Robert Smith, included rarely played songs in their setlist for the festival headlining performance.

The concert featured deep cuts from the band's catalog, including 2 Late, Wrong Number, and Mint Car. These selections represent songs the group performs infrequently during their live shows. The Primavera Sound appearance marked the band's return to the stage after a seven-month break from touring.

cards.headline: Princess Kate Attends Peter Phillips Wedding to Harriet Sperling
cards.teaser: Senior British royals gathered as King Charles' nephew married a nurse in what observers are calling the royal wedding of the summer.
cards.body:
Peter Phillips, the nephew of King Charles and son of Princess Anne, married Harriet Sperling in a ceremony attended by senior members of the British royal family. Princess Kate wore blush tweed to the event, which also drew King Charles and Queen Camilla.

The ceremony marks Phillips' second marriage. Sperling works as a nurse. The wedding brought together a large contingent of the royal family for what has been characterized as a significant social event of the season. Prince William also attended the ceremony alongside his wife.

cards.headline: A24's Backrooms Becomes Studio's Highest Grossing Film Globally
cards.teaser: The horror film is setting an all-time box office record for the independent studio while demonstrating YouTube's growing influence in Hollywood.
cards.body:
A24's horror film Backrooms is becoming the studio's highest-grossing movie at the global box office. The film, based on internet lore, marks a significant achievement for the independent studio behind hits like Everything Everywhere All at Once and Moonlight.

The success of Backrooms alongside the horror release Obsession demonstrates how internet-native content can perform at the theatrical box office, reshaping how Hollywood adapts online material for cinema.

hero.headline: Trump pardons former congressman convicted of insider trading
hero.body:
President Donald Trump issued a full pardon to Steve Buyer, a former Republican congressman from Indiana who was convicted of insider trading in 2023. The White House announced the pardon in a proclamation dated June 4, describing it as a full, complete, and unconditional pardon without providing an explanation for the decision.

Buyer was convicted of using nonpublic information to purchase stocks after leaving office. The former lawmaker served in the House of Representatives representing Indiana before his departure from Congress. His conviction in 2023 followed federal prosecution for securities fraud related to his stock trading activities.

The pardon eliminates the legal consequences of Buyer's conviction, including any remaining penalties or restrictions resulting from his guilty verdict. Presidential pardons are an executive power granted by the Constitution, allowing the president to forgive federal crimes and restore civil rights to those convicted.

This pardon continues a pattern of clemency decisions by Trump, who has previously granted pardons and commutations to political allies and supporters. The lack of explanation in the proclamation follows the standard format for presidential pardons, which are not required to include justification. However, pardons for individuals convicted of financial crimes have historically drawn scrutiny from government ethics observers.

The timing of the pardon, coming more than two years after Buyer's conviction, places it within Trump's current term in office. Former members of Congress who receive pardons for criminal convictions remain ineligible to hold federal office again unless additional steps are taken to restore those specific rights.

cards.headline: U.S. attorney's office in Los Angeles opens investigation into California elections
cards.teaser: Federal prosecutors have launched an investigation into alleged election fraud in California's primary elections.
cards.body:
The U.S. Justice Department sent a federal prosecutor to Los Angeles to observe ballot processing during California's primary elections. The move came as counting continued across the state and delays in results prompted concerns about election integrity.

Donald Trump has made unsubstantiated claims that California Democrats were "rigging" primary races for governor and other statewide offices. State officials have rejected these allegations. The slow ballot count has fueled misinformation about the state's electoral process.

cards.headline: Top White House artificial intelligence adviser to depart administration
cards.teaser: Sriram Krishnan, a central figure in the administration's AI policy efforts, will leave his White House position.
cards.body:
Sriram Krishnan, who has played a central role in the Trump administration's artificial intelligence initiatives, will leave his position at the White House. Krishnan has been the top adviser on AI policy and strategy during his tenure.

Despite his departure from the formal White House role, Krishnan is expected to remain involved in the administration's approach to artificial intelligence technology. His exit comes as the federal government continues to develop policies around AI regulation and development.

cards.headline: Former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: Haaland, who served in the Biden administration, secured the Democratic nomination and could become the first female Native American governor.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland, who served as Interior Secretary under President Biden, won the Democratic primary for governor of New Mexico. Her victory secures the party's nomination ahead of the general election in November.

If elected, Haaland would become the first female Native American governor in the United States. She previously represented New Mexico in Congress before joining the Biden administration.

cards.headline: California governor primary sees Hilton and Becerra leading early returns
cards.teaser: Republican Steve Hilton and Democrat Xavier Becerra are ahead in their respective primaries to replace Governor Gavin Newsom.
cards.body:
Early results in California's gubernatorial primary show Republican Steve Hilton and Democrat Xavier Becerra leading their party races. The primary will determine the nominees to succeed Governor Gavin Newsom, who is not seeking reelection.

On the Democratic side, Becerra faces competition from Katie Porter and Tom Steyer. The Republican field includes Hilton and Chad Bianco, the current Riverside County sheriff. Final results are still being tallied across the state.

cards.headline: Pope Leo criticizes U.S. war with Iran as morally unjustified
cards.teaser: The pontiff said the conflict does not meet Catholic criteria for a just war during his trip to Spain.
cards.body:
Pope Leo XIV said the conflict with Iran fails to meet the criteria for a "just war" under Catholic doctrine. He made these comments while speaking with journalists aboard the papal plane during a six-day visit to Spain.

Catholic just war theory establishes strict requirements for military action to be considered morally acceptable, including legitimate authority, just cause, and proportionality. The pope's statement reflects direct criticism of U.S. military action from one of the world's most influential religious figures.

cards.headline: Analysis examines Justice Alito's use of doubt in constitutional rulings
cards.teaser: A review suggests the Supreme Court justice has employed uncertainty as a tool to limit constitutional protections.
cards.body:
An analysis argues that Justice Samuel Alito has developed a pattern of weaponizing doubt in his constitutional law decisions. The approach has been applied to cases involving reproductive rights, voting rights, and racial equality.

The analysis suggests that by emphasizing uncertainty and questioning established precedents, Alito has contributed to eroding protections in these areas. This judicial strategy may represent a significant part of his legacy on the Supreme Court.
